messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — Elevated 5xx rate detected on streaming-gateway-prod (us-west-2). Metric: streaming.gateway.responses.5xx spiked to 9.8% starting ~10:12Z. Alerts: multiple service keys and customers seeing disconnects. Auto-escalation to oncall. :rotating_light:

Raj: I’m on it — taking primary. Initial check: dashboard shows stream fanout 5xx and connection resets, but paged endpoints (non-streaming) look normal. Customer-facing impact: some long-lived streams are truncating / dropping mid-session.

Emily: Echo — I see a concurrent surge in `streaming.gateway.backpressure` and `streaming.gateway.chunked_errors`. Graphs attached in monitoring. Can someone pull recent gateway logs for the chunked encoder?

Chris: grabbing logs now. quick tail from one affected host:

```
2026-03-15T10:11:58Z gateway[pid=7421] ERROR chunked_encoder: invalid chunk-size header '1g\n'
2026-03-15T10:12:01Z gateway[pid=7421] WARN conn=10.2.5.12: client canceled while streaming
2026-03-15T10:12:05Z gateway[pid=7421] ERROR upstream=backend-3 502 chunked write failed: broken pipe
```

Chris: Looks like malformed chunk sizes are being generated by the gateway output path intermittently. Could be a memory corruption in the encoder or bad upstream encoding negotiation.

Nina: Noted. I’m checking recent deploys — last gateway deploy was 2026-03-15T09:45Z (v1.10.2). No other infra changes. Reproducing locally with high-concurrency stream tests now.

Tom: If chunked encoder is misbehaving, quick mitigation is to route stream traffic to the paged endpoint (non-chunked) for affected customers or toggle gateway config to disable chunked transfer for streams temporarily. Paged path still serves tokens but increases latency/CPU.

Maya: Support update: Customer "AtlasAI" (enterprise) reported 14% of session streams dropped in the last 10m. Case: CS-2391, link: https://support.redwood.internal/tickets/CS-2391. They need an ETA on mitigations.

Raj: Action plan: 1) Hot fallback rule to route streaming requests to paged fallback for impacted routes 2) Collect heap / coredump from gateway host if it recurs 3) Start a canary rollback to v1.10.1 on one AZ to test.

Raj: Implementing fallback via internal routing API now. Command:

```
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routes/override" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_TOKEN" -d '{"selector": "path.startsWith('/v1/streams') && region==\'us-west-2\'", "action": "route_to_paged", "duration_s": 900}'
```

Raj: rule applied. Verifying metrics...

Emily: Early signal — 5xx rate dropping from 9.8% -> 1.4% on us-west-2 within 60s of fallback. Connection resets down too. Looks promising. :white_check_mark:

Chris: I’m still seeing a handful of `client canceled` logs; those could be client-side timeouts triggered by slow fallback path. We should notify CS to expect some transient errors while we stabilize.

Maya: Noted, pinged AtlasAI with temporary mitigation and recommended retry/backoff while we investigate. Also opened a high-priority support bridge.

Nina: Reproducer logs from dev stress test show same chunk-size corruption after ~3000 concurrent streams. Suspect allocator or buffer reuse bug in chunked encoder. Adding sanitizers locally.

Tom: Short-term config tweak we can try: increase `streaming.outbound_write_buffer` to 64k and enable strict chunk validation (drops malformed chunks instead of crashing path). If that reduces malformed chunk output, we can remove fallback earlier.

Chris: Preparing a safe gateway patch: bump buffer + add extra validation in encoder. Will run canary in staging and one AZ in prod (v1.10.3-hotfix).

Raj: Can we keep the fallback for 15–30m while we validate?

Emily: Yes, keep fallback. Also enable verbose chunked-encoder logging on canary nodes to capture full context. Use `CHUNK_DEBUG=1` env var.

Chris: Deploying canary now to us-west-2a with debug logs.

(10m later)

Chris: Canary running — seeing a dramatic reduction in malformed chunk lines on canary host. No coredump so far.

Emily: Metrics: overall 5xx at 0.9% in us-west-2, connection resets down 85% vs peak. Client-cancel events persist at low level (~0.6%) — likely clients timing out while retrying.

Raj: Good. Notify ops and CS: we will keep fallback in place for 30m, monitor, then slowly remove if stable. Oncall handoff: I’ll remain primary for next 45m then hand to Emily for overnight.

Maya: Told AtlasAI we implemented a temporary routing fallback and are testing a hotfix. They asked for a timeline — gave ETA ~2h for full rollback/remediation, monitoring for improvements.

Alice: Product note — check whether any experiment or traffic shaping touched `Transfer-Encoding` headers in the last month. Also add this as a regression test in the streaming E2E suite.

Nina: Collected debug logs and heap profile from canary; uploading to artifacts: https://artifacts.internal/3312/chunk-debug. Added trace IDs for a few affected sessions.

Chris: If hotfix proves stable for 30m, plan: promote v1.10.3-hotfix to remaining AZs, then lift paged fallback. I'll coordinate a quick config roll with infra.

Emily: Post-incident checklist: 1) coredump analysis if occurs 2) add streaming chunk verifier in runtime unit tests 3) add alert link for chunked_errors with runbook 4) follow up with CS for customer RCA.

Raj: Acknowledged. Escalation channel remains this thread. TL;DR: applied paged fallback -> reduced 5xx from ~9.8% to <1%, canary hotfix looks good. Keeping monitoring for 60m.

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE — severity: high; affected: streaming gateway (us-west-2); mitigation: traffic routed to paged fallback; owner: Raj; status: mitigation in place; start_ts=1769991234

Emily: handing oncall to me at +45m per plan. Raj — leave any outstanding artifacts in the handoff note and I’ll carry to full closure.

Raj: Will do. Leaving a list: logs + artifacts link, curl commands used, CS ticket references, canary results. Posting handoff now. :handshake:

(Hand-off posted)

Maya: Thanks team. CS updated AtlasAI and will collect customer logs if needed. Keep me posted for any rollback risk.

Alice: Added one-line entry to product tracker: PROD-STREAM-ENC-REGRESSION.

Emily: Closing loop: if metrics remain stable for 60m we remove fallback and promote hotfix. Otherwise, keep fallback and open full incident RCA.

Chris: ack.

Nina: ack.

Raj: ack; switching my primary token to Emily now.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS UPDATE — mitigation applied, metrics improved, follow-up actions queued.
